page.layout: One printed page of running text, with a faint block of small type below the text (a list of chapter summaries in light type, mostly illegible); no margin notes; catchword and signature absent.

main_text.p: reo sunt, sed melleo colore translucent. In transluci- do fulgor ille melleus Selenitis & Melichrysi spe- ctatur, & in corpore gemmæ est, non in superficie relucet. In aliis pro inclinatione ac situ fulgor variatur & à colore gemmæ divertit.

Pretium autem fecisse & auxisse gemmis raritatem illustri testimonio docet Plinius lib. xxxvii. cap. i. cum de Achate Pyrrhi Regis egisset, addit: Nec deinde alia quæ tradatur, magnopere gemmarum claritas extat apud auctores; præterquam Ismeniam Choraulem, multis fulgentibusque uti solitum, comitante fabula vanitatem eius, indicato in Cypro sex aureis denariis Smaragdo, in quo fuerat sculpta Amymone, iussisse numerari: & cum duo relati essent, imminuto pretio, male me Hercules curatum, dixisse: multum enim detractum gemmæ dignitati.
Cap. v. Tertia ... (summary lines in light type below the text are too faint to transcribe reliably)

page.notes: The lower block of small summary lines (Cap. v. onward, referring to gems and Pliny) is very faint and largely illegible; only the fragment "Cap. v." and "Cap. viii." are reasonably discernible. The head "C. Pli-" is a running signature-like catch line at the end of the text, rendered as printed. No page number, running head, or catchword is visible.
